NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor company, designing cutting-edge GPUs and AI accelerators while relying almost entirely on TSMC's advanced nodes for manufacturing and key memory/networking partners for component supply. Its downstream customer base is dominated by hyperscalers and cloud providers that collectively account for the majority of its data center revenue, giving NVIDIA extraordinary pricing power but also meaningful concentration risk among a handful of large technology customers.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a globally distributed consumer electronics supply chain, fabless in silicon design but deeply dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and a concentrated network of Asian suppliers for displays, memory, and sensors. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily direct-to-consumer and through carriers/retailers, while its high-margin Services segment creates a unique secondary revenue stream from platform partners like Google and app developers who pay to access Apple's ~2 billion active devices.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology is a vertically integrated memory manufacturer sitting at the center of the semiconductor supply chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated group of capital equipment suppliers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its leading-edge DRAM and NAND fabrication. On the demand side, Micron is increasingly exposed to AI-driven hyperscaler spending—particularly for HBM used in NVIDIA GPUs—while also serving diversified end markets including mobile, PC, automotive, and enterprise storage.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings sits at the apex of the semiconductor IP ecosystem, licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP rather than manufacturing silicon, making it almost purely a downstream-driven business where royalty revenues depend on licensee chip shipment volumes across mobile, cloud, automotive, and IoT markets. Its upstream dependencies are relatively lean—centered on EDA software vendors like Cadence and Synopsys—while its downstream reach is extraordinarily broad, with nearly every major fabless and IDM semiconductor company paying ARM royalties on billions of annual chip units.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company positioned between upstream foundry and IP suppliers (primarily TSMC and Arm) and large downstream hyperscaler and networking OEM customers, with its most critical and fast-growing segment being custom AI ASICs and high-speed networking silicon for cloud data centers. The company's strategic pivot toward custom silicon co-design with hyperscalers like AWS and Google makes it increasingly dependent on a concentrated set of high-value downstream customers while leveraging advanced TSMC process nodes for competitive differentiation.
